Lalmohan Ganguli.description: A bachelor and writer of thrillers who serves as Feluda's close friend and sidekick.

Mohinimohan Ganguli.description: Lalmohan Babu's paternal uncle, a practitioner of homoeopathy.

Lalit Mohan Ganguli.description: Lalmohan Babu's great-grandfather, who was a paper merchant and owner of L.M. Ganguli & Sons.

Durgamohan Ganguli.description: Lalmohan Babu's uncle, a former freedom fighter who later became reclusive.

Umashankar Puri.description: The manager of the Rupnarayangarh estate who seeks Feluda's help regarding a potential incident.

Maharaja of Bhagwangarh.description: A royal figure who recommended Feluda to Mr Puri.

Srinath.description: A servant who brings tea and biscuits during Mr Puri's visit.

Raja Chandradeo Singh.description: The former ruler of Rupnarayangarh known for his generosity, who was previously associated with a valuable pendant.

Bhavani Upadhyaya.description: An ayurvedic healer from Haridwar who cured Raja Chandradeo Singh's asthma.

Maharani.description: The wife of Raja Chandradeo Singh, who was aware of the pendant's gifting.

Surajdeo.description: The elder son of Raja Chandradeo Singh, described as kind and bookish, who succeeded his father.

Gorpar.description: A locality in Kolkata, where Lalmohan Babu lives.

Baisakh.description: The first month of the Bengali calendar, marking the Bengali New Year.

Khulna.description: A city now in Bangladesh, mentioned as the location of a historical incident.

Bangladesh.description: A country in South Asia, formerly part of British India and later East Pakistan.

Dhanbad.description: A city in the Indian state of Jharkhand, where Lalmohan Babu's sister is posted.

Durga Puja.description: A major Hindu festival celebrated in Bengal and other parts of India, honoring the goddess Durga.

Rupnarayangarh.description: A fictional or semi-fictional princely state in Uttar Pradesh, central to the story's events.

Uttar Pradesh.description: A large state in northern India, where Rupnarayangarh is located.

Aligarh.description: A city in Uttar Pradesh, referenced as being near Rupnarayangarh.

Haridwar.description: A holy city in Uttarakhand, India, known for its religious significance and as the residence of Bhavani Upadhyaya.

L.M. Ganguli & Sons.description: The family business of Lalmohan Babu's ancestors, a paper merchant shop.

Park Hotel.description: A well-known hotel, presumably in Kolkata, where Mr Puri is staying.

Moradabad.description: A city in Uttar Pradesh, mentioned as Mr Puri's place of origin.

Delhi.description: The capital city of India, where Devishankar studied and started his business.

homoeopathy.description: A system of alternative medicine based on the use of highly diluted substances.

arnica.description: A medicinal herb commonly used in homoeopathy for treating bruises and pain.

rhus tox.description: Short for Rhus toxicodendron, a homeopathic remedy made from poison ivy.

belladonna.description: A plant used in homeopathy, known for its medicinal and toxic properties.

freedom fighter.description: A term used in India for those who participated in the struggle for independence from British rule.

trunk call.description: A long-distance telephone call, especially one made within India.

shikar.description: An Indian term for hunting, especially as a sport among royals.

paisa.description: A unit of currency in India, equal to one-hundredth of a rupee.

Pavandeo Singh.description: The younger son of Raja Chandradeo Singh, interested in photography and filmmaking.

Makhanlal Majumdar.description: An elderly fellow passenger on the Doon Express knowledgeable about pilgrimage sites.

Kantibhai Pandit.description: Bhavani Upadhyaya’s former landlord in Haridwar who provides information about him.

Joginder Ram.description: A friendly Garhwali taxi driver who drives Feluda and his companions.

Hong Kong.description: A city and special administrative region in China, referenced as the place where Feluda bought his recorder.

Hrishikesh.description: A town in Uttarakhand, India, famous for its spiritual and yoga centers.

Doon Express.description: A train service in India connecting Kolkata with Dehradun, passing through several pilgrimage sites.

Badrinath.description: A major Hindu pilgrimage site in Uttarakhand, India, dedicated to Lord Vishnu.

Thar desert.description: A large arid region in northwestern India, known for its sand dunes and camels.

Jamunotri.description: A pilgrimage site in Uttarakhand, India, source of the Yamuna River.

Gangotri.description: A pilgrimage site in Uttarakhand, India, source of the Ganges River.

Gomukh.description: The glacier in Uttarakhand, India, considered the source of the Ganges River.

Panchakedar.description: Refers to the five temples dedicated to Lord Shiva in the Garhwal Himalayas.

Vasukital.description: A high-altitude lake near Kedarnath in Uttarakhand, India.

Himalayas.description: The mountain range in northern India, home to many pilgrimage sites.

Laxman Mohalla.description: A locality in Haridwar where Kantibhai Pandit and Upadhyaya lived.

Singhania.description: A person mentioned as having tried to tempt Upadhyaya.

Hindi.description: The language in which Upadhyaya's postcard was written.

Garhwali.description: Refers to the people and language of the Garhwal region in Uttarakhand.

Garhwal Mandal Vikas Nigam.description: A government-run organization managing tourism and accommodations in Uttarakhand.

Laxmanjhoola.description: A famous suspension bridge and locality near Rishikesh, Uttarakhand.

Jim Corbett.description: A British-Indian hunter and conservationist famous for hunting man-eating tigers and leopards.

The Man-eating Leopard of Rudraprayag.description: A book by Jim Corbett about his hunt for a notorious leopard in Rudraprayag.

Garhwalis.description: The people native to the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand.

Mandakini.description: A river in Uttarakhand, one of the two rivers meeting at Rudraprayag.

Alakananda.description: A river in Uttarakhand, also meeting at Rudraprayag.

Gaurikund.description: A town in Uttarakhand, the base for the trek to Kedarnath temple.

Devprayag.description: A town in Uttarakhand where the Alakananda and Bhagirathi rivers meet to form the Ganges.

Keertinagar.description: A town in Uttarakhand, mentioned as a stop on the way to Rudraprayag.

Srinagar.description: A town in Uttarakhand, capital of the Garhwal district, distinct from Srinagar in Kashmir.

Bartholomew Company.description: A map publishing company, referenced for their map used by Feluda.

Nepal.description: A neighboring country to India, east of Uttarakhand.

Kashmir.description: A region in northern India, west of Uttarakhand.

sanyasi.description: A Hindu ascetic or renunciant who has given up worldly attachments.

ayurveda.description: Ayurveda is an ancient Indian system of medicine based on natural herbs and holistic practices; 'ayurvedic' refers to anything relating to Ayurveda.

ghat.description: A series of steps leading down to a river, often used for bathing or religious rituals.

dharamshala.description: A dharamshala is a rest house or inn, often for pilgrims and usually run by charitable trusts; 'dharamshalas' is the plural form.

Kalikamli dharamshalas.description: A network of well-known dharamshalas in Uttarakhand, run by the Kalikamli trust.

namaskar.description: A respectful Indian greeting, similar to 'hello' or 'greetings'.

Mr Giridhari.description: The hospitable manager of the rest house in Rudraprayag, fond of Bengali literature.

Krishnakant Bhargav.description: A journalist in Rudraprayag who recognizes Feluda and is writing a story about Bhavani Upadhyaya.

Rudraprayag.description: A town in Uttarakhand, India, known for its religious significance and scenic beauty.

Corbett.description: Refers to Jim Corbett, the famous British-Indian hunter and conservationist known for killing man-eating leopards and tigers.

Calcutta.description: Now called Kolkata, a major city in eastern India.

Allahabad.description: A city in Uttar Pradesh, India, now officially known as Prayagraj.

Kedarnath.description: Kedarnath is a prominent Hindu temple town in the Himalayas, dedicated to Lord Shiva and a major pilgrimage site in Uttarakhand. 'Kedar' is a common abbreviation for Kedarnath.

Badri.description: Short for Badrinath, another important Hindu pilgrimage site in Uttarakhand.

Australian.description: Refers to Australia, here indicating the nationality of the television company.

Royal Bengal tiger.description: A subspecies of tiger native to the Indian subcontinent, known for its beauty and power.

chamchas.description: A Hindi slang term meaning 'sycophants' or 'flatterers', often used for followers or hangers-on.

Nepali mask.description: A traditional decorative mask from Nepal, often used in cultural or religious contexts.

Travancore.description: A historical princely state in southern India, referenced as the original owner of the pendant.

Agastyamuni.description: A town in Uttarakhand, India, noted for its elevation and as a stop on the journey.

Guptakashi.description: A town in Uttarakhand, famous for its temples and as a stop en route to Kedarnath.

Son Prayag.description: A location where the Son Ganga river joins Mandakini, en route to Kedarnath.

Son Ganga.description: A river joining Mandakini at Son Prayag.

Rajasthani.description: Relating to Rajasthan, a state in India; here, refers to a traditional cap.

Chandrasekhar Mahadev.description: A temple in Guptakashi dedicated to Lord Shiva.

Ardhanarishwar.description: A temple in Guptakashi dedicated to the composite form of Shiva and Parvati.

Ukhimath.description: A town in Uttarakhand where the winter worship of Kedareshwar is held.

Kedareshwar.description: A form of Lord Shiva worshipped at Kedarnath and Ukhimath.

Baikuntha Mallik.description: A poet admired by Lalmohan Babu, who wrote about Kedarnath.

babu.description: Babu is a respectful term of address in India, often used for educated men or gentlemen, especially in Bengal.

dandi.description: A dandi is a type of palanquin or sedan chair used for carrying people, especially on mountain treks; 'dandis' is the plural form.

kandi.description: A basket-like carrier used to transport people, typically in hilly regions.

panda.description: A panda is a local priest or guide who provides lodging and assistance to pilgrims, especially in Haridwar; 'pandas' is the plural form.

jalebis.description: A sweet, deep-fried Indian dessert made from flour and soaked in syrup.

kachauris.description: A savory, deep-fried Indian snack stuffed with lentils or spices.

puja.description: A Hindu ritual of worship, often performed daily in temples.

Ramwara.description: A resting place on the way to Kedarnath, known for its dharamshalas and scenic beauty.

Mahabharata.description: An ancient Indian epic that narrates the story of the Kurukshetra War and the fates of the Kaurava and Pandava princes.

Yudhishthir.description: A central character in the Mahabharata, known for his righteousness and leadership among the Pandavas.

Bengalis.description: People from Bengal, a region in eastern India and Bangladesh.

darshan.description: A spiritual viewing or auspicious sighting, especially of a deity or sacred place.

deo-dekhni.description: A brief, special glimpse of a deity or temple, considered auspicious.

Hotel Himlok.description: A local hotel in Kedarnath mentioned as being full upon the group's arrival.

Birla guest house.description: A guest house in Kedarnath, likely funded or managed by the Birla family, a prominent Indian industrialist family.

Kali Kamliwali dharamshala.description: A charitable rest house in Kedarnath, often run by religious trusts to provide affordable lodging for pilgrims.

Benaras.description: Also known as Varanasi, a holy city in India on the banks of the Ganges, famous for its temples and spiritual significance.

Jai Kedar.description: A religious exclamation meaning 'Victory to Kedar (Shiva)', commonly used by pilgrims at Kedarnath.

Chorabalital.description: Chorabalital, now known as Gandhi Sarovar, is a glacial lake near Kedarnath from which the Mandakini river originates.

razais.description: Thick, quilted blankets commonly used in North India for warmth.

Sarovar.description: A Hindi word meaning 'lake', often used for sacred or significant lakes in India.

Baba.description: A respectful term for an elderly man or ascetic, often used for holy men in India.

Chaliye.description: A Hindi word meaning 'let's go' or 'please proceed'.

Vermillion.description: A bright red powder (also called 'sindoor' or 'kumkum') used in Hindu rituals and as a mark on the forehead.

Mr Singhania.description: A wealthy and powerful businessman involved in the pursuit of a valuable pendant; he tries to persuade Feluda to help him acquire it.

Mr Mitter.description: A private detective and the protagonist of the stories, known for his intellect and investigative skills.

Topshe.description: Feluda’s younger cousin and the narrator of the stories, present during the events in Kedarnath.

Maharaja of Travancore.description: The former royal ruler of the princely state of Travancore in southern India, indicating the pendant's prestigious origin.

goondas.description: A Hindi term for thugs or criminals.

Devishankar Puri.description: The son of Umashankar Puri, who was a child during the events described.

saffron.description: A color often associated with Hindu monks and ascetics, symbolizing renunciation and spirituality.

devnagari.description: A script used for several Indian languages, including Hindi and Sanskrit.

Bengali.description: A language spoken in the Bengal region of South Asia, including Bangladesh and the Indian state of West Bengal.

Durga.description: A major Hindu goddess, symbolizing power and protection.

Gangopadhyaya.description: A Bengali surname, often anglicized as 'Ganguly'.

pendant.description: An ornamental piece of jewelry that hangs from a chain worn around the neck.

Kaka.description: A Hindi/Bengali term meaning 'uncle', used to address one's paternal uncle.

bank locker.description: A secure storage facility provided by banks for valuables.
